=== 829dfeb8c1 Refuse printer tool calls that do not fit the conversation
Every printer conversation is offered all eight printer tools, so the tool
list stays the same for the prompt cache, but nothing checked that a call
fit the conversation. printer_add in a Change conversation saved a second
printer and moved the conversation onto it, and printer_change took any
saved printer's name, even in an Add conversation before anything was
added. Test runs showed models calling printer_add and printer_identify in
Change conversations.

PrinterConversation::preflight_tool, which runs before any card, now
refuses, with an error that says where to go instead:
- printer_identify, printer_add and printer_manual_setup outside an Add
  conversation (not_in_this_conversation: another printer is added with
  + Add printer on Home);
- printer_change before the conversation has a printer (no_printer), and on
  a printer other than the one it is about (other_printer, or
  unknown_printer for a name that is not saved).
change() no longer repeats the name check.

The tool list is not scoped per mode. Hiding a tool does not stop a call,
so the refusal is needed either way, and a restricted-but-stable list
(tool_choice allowed_tools) exists only on some providers. The docs said
otherwise: mcp-tool-extension-guide.md still described one tool per mode,
a design reversed on 2026-09-23 (8334b3395b) whose reason, the pinned
printer card, was removed on 2026-09-22. It and architecture.md now describe
the eight tools and the refusals, and the guide's tool table lists all eight.

tests/printer_prompt answers the tools with the same refusals and adds
change-add-another ("I also have a Prusa MK4S, can you add it too?"): nothing
is ever added; the reply said where to add it in 15 of 20 runs on DeepSeek
V4 Flash and 9 to 15 of 20 with --app, often "Yes, I can add it" with no
tool called at all. The next commit addresses that in the prompt.

Verified: agent_bridge_tests 265 cases pass, with new cases for each
refusal and a host test that the refusal reaches the model; AgentUI 213
pass; shell_harness --printer-live 0 failures.

agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:442:**Seeing and exporting (M6).** A tool activity may carry a `ToolImage` (base64 PNG or JPEG, capped at 1280 px and 2 MB) that is never persisted; the MCP projection appends an `image` content block (the bridge passes it through on every protocol version), and the OpenAI projection follows the function output with a user message holding an `input_image`, both tested. `view_render` calls `GLCanvas3D::render_thumbnail` with the main 3MF thumbnail's parameters (the plate's printable parts, no bed) and Orca's `Camera::ViewAngleType`, and encodes with `GCodeThumbnails::compress_thumbnail`; it refuses before the canvas is initialized, as the archive export does. Preview mode is not built. `project_attachment_read` reads only a relative path inside the attachment folder, outside `JusPrin/` and `.thumbnails/`; larger pictures are scaled and re-encoded with `wxImage`, text is cut at 32 KB. `slice_inspect` rebuilds the preview's layer split from `GCodeProcessorResult::moves` (the stored result has no layer list or layer times) and pages the plate's G-code file by line. `activity_cancel` is computation-only: a pending proposal through the coordinator's own cancel, the tools' slice through `Plater::cancel_slicing` (the notification's Cancel, which returns once the run stopped; the snapshot's running flag clears a moment later), and a tools' job through the worker's cancel, whose end is read from the jobs list. `export_file` writes G-code by copying the plate's slicer output (Orca's own export adds only post-processing scripts and removable-media handling, which this does not run), sliced and project 3MF through `Plater::export_3mf` with `Silence` (so the open project keeps its name and path), STL from the parts' raw meshes as placed (negative volumes are not subtracted), and presets through `PresetBundle::export_current_configs` with system presets included, because the presets in use are usually system presets with edits and Orca's menu would write nothing for them. `slice_start` takes `wait`, and `slice_report` an `intent` section that measures the slice against intent answers naming a time, a weight or a cost. If the model tries to add a printer from a conversation about a printer that is already set up (a "Change" or "Connect" conversation), the app refuses the tool call, saves nothing, and tells the model where adding is done. The problems are elsewhere: a later commit removed three printer tools, and two design docs and one code comment still describe them. I read the diffs and the current code but did not run any tests.

## How the refusal works

Three commits on `jusprin-newui` built this:

- **829dfeb8c1** added the refusal to `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` ([PrinterConversation.cpp:297](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:297)), which runs before any tool call executes. Every printer conversation is offered the same tools so the prompt cache stays valid, so the check has to happen when a call arrives. Outside an Add conversation:
  - `printer_identify` and `printer_add` are refused with the code `not_in_this_conversation`. The message tells the model to point the person to "+ Add printer on Home". That button exists at [HomeUI App.tsx:114](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/App.tsx:114).
  - `printer_change` is refused unless it names the conversation's own printer. It returns `other_printer` for another saved printer and `unknown_printer` for a name that isn't saved. In an Add conversation that has not added a printer yet, it returns `no_printer`.
- **2f8afe107a** fixed a gap the refusal can't reach. Sometimes the model answered "Yes, I can add it" without calling any tool, so nothing reached the check. The Change/Connect prompt now says another printer is not added here and names the Home button. In 20 test runs on DeepSeek V4 Flash, the model said where to add the printer 20 times, up from 15.
- **b60fc2d8e6** removed `printer_manual_setup`, `printer_manual_connection` and `printer_setup_finish`, and dropped `printer_manual_setup` from the refusal list. That is correct, since the tool is gone. The person can still open OrcaSlicer's full printer list from a page button, but only in an Add conversation before a printer exists ([App.tsx:430](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:430), [App.tsx:446](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:446)), so that button can't switch a Change conversation onto another printer either.

Test coverage:
- **Unit test:** [test_printer_conversation.cpp:616](tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:616) checks every refusal in both Change and Connect conversations, and that nothing is added or changed.
- **Host test:** [test_printer_conversation.cpp:1446](tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:1446) checks that the refusal reaches the model as an error mentioning "+ Add printer on Home", and that the conversation stays on its original printer.
- **Prompt harness:** `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py:674` returns the same refusal text when the model tries to add.

## What's out of date after b60fc2d8e6

1. **The design docs still describe eight tools and list the removed ones.** There are now five.
   - [architecture.md:137](agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md:137) says "the eight printer tools".
   - [mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) says "eight" at lines 95 and 289. Its tool table still has rows for `printer_manual_connection` (360), `printer_manual_setup` (361, including "refused outside an Add conversation") and `printer_setup_finish` (363).
2. **A code comment describes a tool that no longer exists.** [App.tsx:403](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:403) says the model's `printer_setup_finish` closes the panel when the person is done. Now only the person's own Back/close action closes it. The comment should be updated. It's also worth confirming that closing the panel works without that tool.

One small point that isn't a bug: the prompt harness returns `unknown_printer` for any wrong name, never `other_printer`. That is consistent because each test case has only one saved printer, but the harness never tests the "another saved printer" case.

I can fix the docs and the comment and run the `agent_bridge_tests` and AgentUI test suites if you'd like.

The app decides the tools -- the eight printer tools, the same in every mode -- checks every call, refuses one that does not fit the conversation (adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one it is about), and refuses a turn that has no instructions rather than falling back to the project assistant's prompt. It posts the opening once per session, and a tap's note only when the tap goes through, bounded to 2 KB. It still writes the notes for what only it can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, its model id is not on the list, or a save or undo failed.
----

  So the cost of a definition is what it adds to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn, and the budget stays a trigger rather than a gate. What would change that reading: a catalog large enough to make the first request of every conversation expensive on its own, or transcripts showing the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch both; neither has appeared yet.
- **The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set.** Home's printer panel runs its own conversation (`PrinterConversation`), offered the eight printer tools and no others, the same list in every mode, so the list stays byte-identical across a conversation and across conversations of the same mode. What a call may do depends on the conversation, and `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses the rest before any card, with an error that says where to go instead: finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`, `printer_manual_setup`) only in an Add conversation, since a Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has and an add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it; `printer_change` only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one; the connection tools only once there is a saved printer. A list that differs by mode is not used: the conversation's own refusal is needed whatever the model is shown, and a restricted-but-stable list (`tool_choice` with `allowed_tools`) exists only on some providers. What would change that: transcripts of the model reaching for a refused tool and not recovering, which `tests/printer_prompt` measures (`change-add-another`). Until 2026-09-23 the panel offered one tool per mode (7f66e75b07), to keep a lookup from clearing the pinned card of the printer a Change session was about; that card is gone (4d4f9e466b), and one tool per step left an Add conversation with no tool to connect the printer it had just added (8334b3395b). The app decides the tools; the words are the page's (`AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` for the instructions, `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts` for the notes the model reads after a tap), and a turn the page has not yet written them for is refused rather than sent with the project assistant's prompt. The Add instructions carry the whole printer list, about 28 KB, which caches as a fixed prefix. No printer conversation carries the project: no workspace in the turn, none in a tool result.
- **Deferral, when the measurements say so.** Use the platform's own deferral, never a hand-rolled switcher. On the in-app side that is OpenAI's `tool_search` with `defer_loading: true` on the Responses API, documented for `gpt-5.4` and later; support on the pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` is unverified. On the MCP side clients defer on their own, as Claude Code does. Toolsets are the deferral unit, and OpenAI recommends fewer than ten functions per namespace. An enable-toolset tool that rewrites the tools array breaks the prompt cache on every switch and is not to be built.
- **Shape each tool as a domain operation.** A tool does one thing a slicer user would name: place an object, lay out the plates, mark a region, set up the printer. Not a wrapper per Orca function, and not an interpreter for a list of unrelated commands. Optional facets of one operation are fine when each is independently typed and conflicting facets are rejected.
----
- attachment-based import (`object_import`) is in-app-only, and path-based `object_import_file` is MCP-only, because a file reaches the app through the conversation in one case and through an approved path in the other; that is two honest definitions over one workspace command, not one tool with forked behavior; and
- a future MCP diagnostics tool may be MCP-only if it exists to establish the external connection; and
- the printer panel's eight tools carry only the `Printer` exposure: neither adapter lists them, and the panel's conversation offers all of them in every mode and refuses what does not fit it (see "Tool budget and tool shape"). They take no `planId` (`joins_plans` excludes them), and what the model reads back from them is the tool's own result, not the host's workspace envelope.

Document the reason beside the registry definition and test it. Exposure is not a place to fork behavior: if two adapters need different semantics, they need a better shared command or honestly separate definitions.

The refusal didn't fire because there was nothing to refuse: the conversation was an Add conversation from its first message. The model never switched from changing a printer to adding one. The app did that on purpose when the panel opened, because the printer your project selected is Bambu's stock profile, not one of your saved printers.

## Is the printer from the .3mf or your local settings?

It comes from the .3mf. The file's `Metadata/project_settings.config` names the printer profile `printer_settings_id = "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle"`, which is the stock Bambu Lab system profile. When the project opens, OrcaSlicer selects that stock profile. I checked the running app with `workspace_inspect`, and its selected printer preset is `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`.

That stock profile is not your saved printer. Your saved one is `Bambu Lab A1 mini 2.json` in `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/user/default/machine/`, which is built on top of the stock profile but is a separate preset. The header still says "Bambu Lab A1 mini" because, for a stock profile, the header shows the profile's model name ([SetupCommands.cpp:99](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp:99)). So the header looks the same whether the selected printer is saved or stock.

## Why you got the "Which printer do you have?" conversation

1. "Printer settings…" in the header menu passes that label, "Bambu Lab A1 mini", as the printer name and asks for a Change conversation ([PrinterMenu.cpp:174](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp:174)).
2. `PrinterConversation::start` finds no saved printer with that name and quietly switches the conversation to Add mode, on purpose ([PrinterConversation.cpp:164](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:164)). Its comment says "A printer this app has not saved cannot be changed … Adding one is what there is to do." This dates from 8334b3395b (2026-09-23).
3. The refusals only apply to Change and Connect conversations, so in Add mode `printer_add` is allowed. It saved `Qidi X-Plus 4 (2).json` today at 16:20:44.

This is a design gap, not a failure of the refusal. You asked for the settings of the printer on screen, and the app sent you into adding a printer without saying why. I haven't changed any code for it. Possible directions:

- **Point to the saved printer:** say that the project uses Bambu's stock A1 mini profile, and offer to switch to your saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2".
- **Warn before adding:** keep the Add conversation, but open it with a note that the selected printer isn't one of your saved printers.
- **Open the settings instead:** for a stock profile, skip the conversation and open OrcaSlicer's own printer settings.

Tell me which one you want and I'll reproduce it in an isolated test copy of the app first.
